question.problem: A cyclist accelerates with a constant acceleration from $2\,\text{m/s}$ to $12\,\text{m/s}$ in $4$ seconds. Find their acceleration.
question.worked_solution:
We can find the acceleration of an object by computing the slope of its speed-time graph.  To plot a speed-time graph, we need two points.

- The cyclist starts at a speed of $2\,\text{m/s}.$ This corresponds to the point $(0,2).$

- In $4$ seconds, the cyclist reaches a speed of $12\,\text{m/s}.$ This corresponds to the point $(4,12).$

Since the acceleration is constant, we plot the two points and draw a line through them as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945962/assets/d1a813ebcbfa04b42729d60b73bc439a2060aafae8430c60984ba1772e940364.png)

The slope of the cyclist's speed-time graph gives their acceleration. The slope of this line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{12\text{ m/s}-2\text{ m/s}}{4\text{s}-0\text{s}} \\  & =\frac{10\text{ m/s}}{4\text{ s}} \\  & =2.5\,\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the cyclist's acceleration is $2.5\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$
